messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: force=T and fit.ProbeLevelModel
parts:
Hi,
If I do
> fit(plm,force=T)
then it only forces a refit for the unfit probes (so no forced of
refitting), because units is (by default) 'remaining'. So in terms of
which units are fit, it is equivalent to
> fit(plm)
(I realize it is different in whether the cached units are reread,
etc.) This wasn't the behavior I was expecting -- I thought
fit(plm,force=T) and fit(plm,units=NULL,force=T) would be the same,
namely all of the units would be forced to be refit.

I haven't thought of all the ins and outs of whether I think this
should be the desired behavior (I guess it could be useful to be able
to fit only the remaining units but make sure that the cached data is
reread), but the documentation isn't clear as to what happens in this
case. So if this behavior is intended, it would be helpful to have
this highlighted under the description of the arguments because I had
to read the code to understand what the problem was.

Best,
Elizabeth

>From documentation:

fit(this, units="remaining", ..., force=FALSE, ram=moreUnits,
verbose=FALSE, moreUnits=1)

Arguments:

units: The units to be fitted. If 'NULL', all units are considered.
If 'remaining', only non-fitted units are considered.

...: Arguments passed to '*readUnits()'.

force: If 'TRUE', already fitted units are re-fitted, and cached
data is re-read.

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] force=T and fit.ProbeLevelModel
parts:
Hi.

In general for all methods, argument units=NULL defaults to *all*
units. The same should go for other kind of indices, e.g.
indices=NULL. If you find cases where this is not the case, please
let me know.

Now to argument 'force': It takes TRUE or FALSE, which provides
little granularity. The use of 'force' was first used to forced
processing of the parts in the method, but not of methods called
internally. I've recently started to pass down 'force' to all
internal methods/cases where it applies. I've been thinking of making
'force' into an integer instead, so that you can tell how deeply you
want 'force' to be applied. If you just want to refit a unit, you
might not want to pass down 'force' to the method extracting CDF cell
indices. Again, this is on the to do list, and for now you should
expect that 'force' is passed down recursively where it makes sense.

Now to fit(plm, force=TRUE): Force applies to the units requested.
Since 'units' defaults to "remaining", it only applies, as you
noticed, to remaining units, and it makes little sense to ask fit() to
force fitting of these units since they are going to be fitted anyway,
thus fit(plm, force=TRUE) and fit(plm, force=FALSE) fit the same units
(given that the CDF hasn't changed which shouldn't happen).

I'm very reluctant to give add rules on interpretation of default
arguments conditioned on the value of others. Number of one rule I
stick to is that you should get the same thing if you write out the
argument explicitly or not. I never utilize missing(). So

fit(plm, force=TRUE)
fit(plm, units="remaining", force=TRUE)

must be identical. So you question boils down to what:

fit(plm, units="remaining", force=TRUE)

should do. First step is to document it, if it is confusing. Could
you please forward me the Rd help text you want me add?

FEI: In general, the Rd help pages lag behind. For development usage
of the package the code is the number one documentation. In
appreciate any contributions (as close to valid Rd format as possible,
please) to help pages, especially obvious ones. Otherwise, the
aroma.affymetrix group page is the number one source of documentation
that should be fairly up to date. One way to have additional text
added to these, is to click on "Discuss this page" at the bottom and
be as precise as possible on what to update/add. Ready
cut'n'paste-able sentences/paragraphs are more likely to be updated.

Cheers

Henrik
